what_it_does: Mamba2 is a type of neural network that processes sequences (like text or audio) using a mathematical structure called a state-space model rather than the attention mechanism used in transformers. It is memory-bound, meaning the bottleneck is how fast data can be moved around rather than how fast arithmetic can be done, because its computations involve lots of element-wise multiplications with values that are broadcast (repeated) across many positions in irregular patterns. Standard processors (CPUs and GPUs) handle this inefficiently. This paper builds a custom overlay processor — a reconfigurable compute engine — on an FPGA (a programmable chip that can be wired up in different ways after manufacture) specifically to run Mamba2 efficiently. Three ideas are combined: fusing multiple operations into a single pass over the data to avoid loading it repeatedly; skipping over groups of near-zero values (sparsity — treating unimportant numbers as zero to save work); and using a reconfigurable grid of small multiply-add units (a systolic array — a tiled arrangement where partial results flow between neighbors like a conveyor belt) that can be reconfigured for different Mamba2 operations.
